backlog.spec: Train the model on a random 90% subset of the training data (different subset per fold if possible, but since the harness handles folds, just use 90% within fit_predict).
backlog.title: Subsampling training data

backlog.spec: Weight the training samples by the inverse frequency of their class in the train_y vector.

backlog.spec: Apply StandardScaler to the fingerprint matrix before passing it to the RandomForestClassifier.

backlog.spec: Use an intermediate radius or a specific RDKit behavior if available, but since RADIUS is int, stick to 3 as a 'larger' step.

backlog.spec: Set `class_weight='balanced'` in the RandomForestClassifier.
backlog.title: Class Weight adjustment

backlog.spec: Calculate the number of bits set in the fingerprints and add as a feature (L1 norm).
backlog.title: Custom Minkowski Distance (Feature Engineering)

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with early stopping (using a validation set split inside fit_predict) to find the optimal number of iterations.
backlog.title: Early Stopping with LightGBM

backlog.title: Random Forest Ensemble

backlog.spec: Apply a logit transformation to the target variable y before training to handle potential class imbalance or skew, and then inverse-transform the predicted probabilities to the [0, 1] range.
backlog.title: Logit Transform on Target

backlog.spec: Before training, apply sklearn.feature_selection.VarianceThreshold(threshold=0.01) to the featurized matrix to remove constant or near-constant Morgan bits.
backlog.title: Feature Variance Thresholding

backlog.spec: Reduce N_BITS from 2048 to 1024 to force the model to generalize on more important bits and reduce the feature space dimensionality.
backlog.title: Reduced Fingerprint Size

backlog.spec: Implement a simple bootstrap subsampling in fit_predict where only 80% of the training data is used for each fit to improve generalization and speed up training.
backlog.title: Subsample Training

backlog.spec: Calculate class weights based on the distribution of train_y and pass the 'class_weight' parameter to the RandomForestClassifier.
backlog.title: Class Weight Balancing

backlog.spec: Increase the Morgan fingerprint RADIUS from 2 to 3 to capture larger structural environments, while keeping N_BITS at 2048.
backlog.title: Morgan Radius 3

backlog.spec: Use lightgbm.LGBMClassifier with 500 estimators and a validation set to implement early stopping. Since fit_predict doesn't provide a clean validation set, use the last 10% of train_smiles for this purpose.
backlog.title: LightGBM with Early Stopping

backlog.spec: Use StandardScaler from scikit-learn to normalize the RDKit descriptor block (MolWt, MolLogP, NumHDonors) before concatenating with the Morgan fingerprints. This helps if the scale of descriptors (like MolWt being in the hundreds) dominates the binary fingerprint bits.
backlog.title: Standardize Descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForest with XGBClassifier. Set max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, and colsample_bytree=0.8. This combines the shallow-tree finding with more robust regularization.
backlog.title: XGBoost with Heavy Regularization

backlog.spec: Apply a logit-like transformation or a simple sigmoid scaling to the target y values if they are treated as probabilities, though since they are binary, consider using the 'predict_proba' output and checking if a calibration (like Platt scaling) improves the AUC.
backlog.title: Logit Transform Target

backlog.spec: Apply VarianceThreshold to the combined feature set (Morgan bits + RDKit descriptors) to remove bits that are constant or near-constant across the training set. This can reduce noise and speed up training.
backlog.title: Feature Selection via Variance Threshold

backlog.spec: Calculate the class weights of the training set and pass them to the RandomForestClassifier (or XGB/LightGBM) using the 'class_weight' or 'scale_pos_weight' parameter to handle potential imbalance in blood-brain barrier penetration data.
backlog.title: Class Weight Balancing

backlog.spec: Increase the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3. This captures larger local environments of atoms, which may be important for identifying complex scaffolds that cross the blood-brain barrier.
backlog.title: Morgan Radius 3

backlog.spec: Reduce the Morgan fingerprint size from 2048 bits to 1024 bits. This acts as a form of dimensionality reduction and might prevent the model from over-indexing on sparse, noisy bits in a small dataset (1624 molecules).
backlog.title: Reduced Fingerprint Size

backlog.spec: Train three separate RandomForestClassifiers with different seeds (or different max_features) and average their predict_proba results. This is a manual implementation of Bagging to reduce variance.
backlog.title: Manual RF Ensemble

backlog.spec: Implement a simple bootstrapping approach where each fold's training set is sampled with replacement (e.g., 80% of the available training data). This can improve generalization on small datasets.
backlog.title: Subsample Training

backlog.spec: Use XGBClassifier with the early_stopping_rounds parameter. This requires an internal validation split during the fit_predict call, which can help find the optimal number of iterations automatically.
backlog.title: XGBoost Early Stopping

backlog.spec: Instead of a 0.5/0.5 average of the probabilities from RandomForestClassifier and XGBClassifier, implement a weighted average. Specifically, use a weight of 0.6 for the XGBClassifier and 0.4 for the RandomForestClassifier, as boosting models often capture the underlying distribution better than RF in small datasets.
backlog.title: Weighted Ensemble of RF and XGBoost

backlog.spec: Calculate the ratio of negative to positive samples in the training set (count(y=0) / count(y=1)) and pass this as the 'scale_pos_weight' parameter to the XGBClassifier. This helps handle potential class imbalance in the 1624 molecules.
backlog.title: XGBoost with Scale_pos_weight

backlog.spec: Apply a sigmoid-like transform to the binary labels (or use a logit-style mapping for the probability space) before training and then transform the probabilities back. Since the target is binary, this is better implemented by using a CrossEntropy loss internally in a way that mimics logit scaling, but given the constraints, a simple sigmoid-based scaling of the 0/1 labels can be tried.
backlog.title: Logit Transform on Target

backlog.spec: Expand the RDKit descriptor block in the featurize function. In addition to MolWt, MolLogP, and NumHDonors, add Descriptors.TPSA(m) and Descriptors.NumRotBonds(m) to the feature vector concatenated with the Morgan fingerprint.
backlog.title: Add TPSA and RotatableBondCount

backlog.spec: Since the harness doesn't provide a validation set easily, simulate a small internal validation set (e.g., 10% of training data) to find the optimal number of boosting rounds (n_estimators) for XGBoost, then use that fixed number for the final fit.
backlog.title: XGBoost early stopping emulation

backlog.spec: Instead of averaging the raw probabilities from the RandomForestClassifier and XGBClassifier, rank the test molecules by the probability returned by each model. The final predicted probability is the average of the two rank-positions mapped back to a probability space (or simply average the ranks), which can be more robust to outliers.
backlog.title: Rank Averaging Ensemble

backlog.spec: Reduce MAX_FEATURES from 0.3 to 0.15 for the RandomForestClassifier to increase the diversity of the trees, potentially leading to a more robust ensemble when blended with XGBoost.
backlog.title: Feature Subsampling for RF

backlog.spec: Implement a basic Balanced Random Forest logic by subsampling the training data for each tree in the RandomForestClassifier. For each tree, take a random subset of the minority and majority classes to ensure each tree sees a balanced distribution.
backlog.title: Balanced Random Forest

backlog.spec: Reduce N_BITS from 2048 to 1024 while keeping RADIUS at 2. This acts as a form of dimensionality reduction/regularization, forcing the model to prioritize the most significant structural bits.
backlog.title: Morgan Fingerprint Bit Squeezing

backlog.spec: Train a third model (e.g., a small Random Forest) that takes the probability outputs of the current RF and XGBoost as its input features, then use this 'meta-model' to make the final prediction for the test set.
backlog.title: Multi-Model Probability Stacking

backlog.spec: Instead of averaging the raw probabilities of the RF and XGBoost models, convert each probability to a binary class (using a 0.5 threshold), and then average the results. Alternatively, since we need a single probability return, use a soft-rank approach: if both models agree on the class, return the average probability; if they disagree, return the probability of the model that had the higher confidence (further from 0.5).
backlog.title: Rank Averaging Ensemble

backlog.spec: Calculate the ratio of negative to positive samples in the training set (sum(y==0) / sum(y==1)) and pass this as the 'scale_pos_weight' parameter to the XGBClassifier. This helps handle potential class imbalance in the blood-brain barrier dataset.
backlog.title: Scale_pos_weight for XGBoost

backlog.spec: Apply a sigmoid-like transformation to the target labels (though they are binary 0/1, we can treat them as probabilities or use a logit-based weight) or, more effectively, use a custom objective function for XGBoost that mimics the log-loss but with a learning rate schedule that decays over iterations.
backlog.title: Logit Transform Target

backlog.spec: Reduce the N_BITS from 2048 to 1024. Sometimes a smaller, more compressed fingerprint prevents the model from over-focusing on noise bits in a small dataset (1624 molecules).
backlog.title: Reduced Fingerprint Size

backlog.spec: Since we cannot use the native early stopping API easily without a validation set in fit_predict, implement a manual loop for XGBoost training. Train for 1000 iterations, but keep track of the best performance on a small internal 80/20 split of the training data and 'roll back' to the best iteration's weights.
backlog.title: XGBoost Early Stopping Emulation

backlog.spec: Use StandardScaler from sklearn to normalize the RDKit descriptors (MolWt, MolLogP, NumHDonors) before concatenating them with the Morgan fingerprint bits. This ensures that the large magnitude of MolWt doesn't dominate the gradient updates compared to the 0/1 bits.
backlog.title: Standardize Descriptors

backlog.spec: Train both the RandomForest and XGBoost models on a bootstrap sample of the training data (e.g., 80% of the data with replacement). Use the out-of-bag samples to help stabilize the ensemble's generalization.
backlog.title: Subsample Training

backlog.spec: Expand the RDKit descriptor block to include TPSA (Topological Polar Surface Area) and NumRotBonds (Number of Rotatable Bonds) in addition to the existing MolWt, MolLogP, and NumHDonors.
backlog.title: Add TPSA and RotatableBondCount

backlog.spec: Apply a small temperature scaling to the final probabilities. Instead of 0.5 * (P1 + P2), use 0.5 * (P1^k + P2^k) / (P1^k + P2^k + 1) or a similar calibration to push the probabilities away from the 0.5 center toward the 0/1 extremes.
backlog.title: Probability Scaling

backlog.spec: Reduce the XGBClassifier max_depth from 3 to 2. In small datasets, very shallow trees are often more robust against overfitting to specific molecular scaffolds.
backlog.title: Reduce XGBoost Max Depth

backlog.spec: Instead of averaging the probabilities of the RandomForest and XGBoost models, convert the probabilities to ranks (e.g., using a simple linear mapping to 1-N) and average the ranks before converting back to a probability-like score. This helps mitigate the impact of one model being overconfident.
backlog.title: Rank Averaging Ensemble

backlog.spec: Transform the output probabilities of the RandomForest and XGBoost into logits using the sigmoid function's inverse: log(p/(1-p)). Average these logits, then pass the result through a sigmoid function to get the final probability. This is often more robust than averaging probabilities directly.
backlog.title: Logit-Space Averaging

backlog.spec: Calculate the density of set bits in the Morgan fingerprint (number of bits set divided by N_BITS) as an additional descriptor feature. This provides a global structural metric that the model can use to distinguish between sparse and dense molecules.
backlog.title: Add Bit-Density Feature

backlog.spec: Manually implement a balanced random forest approach by subsampling the training data for each tree (or for the RF model as a whole) to ensure that the minority class is oversampled or the majority class is undersampled, ensuring the model doesn't become biased towards the majority class.
backlog.title: Balanced Random Forest Logic

backlog.spec: Reduce the MAX_FEATURES hyperparameter for the RandomForestClassifier from 0.3 to 0.15. This forces the trees to be more decorrelated by only allowing them to see a smaller subset of the features at each split, which can improve ensemble diversity.
backlog.title: Reduced Max Features for RF

backlog.spec: Calculate the ratio of negative samples to positive samples in the training set (sum(y==0)/sum(y==1)) and pass this as the scale_pos_weight parameter to the XGBClassifier. This helps handle class imbalance directly during the boosting process.
backlog.title: XGBoost Scale_pos_weight

backlog.spec: Since true early stopping is hard with these APIs, simulate it by training XGBoost for a high number of rounds (e.g., 1000) but use a very small learning_rate (e.g., 0.01) and a smaller max_depth to prevent overshooting and over-training.
backlog.title: Early Stopping Emulation

backlog.spec: The RDKit descriptors (MolWt, MolLogP, etc.) have very different scales. Use a simple Z-score normalization (subtract mean, divide by std dev) on the RDKit descriptor block only before concatenating with the Morgan fingerprint bits.
backlog.title: Standardize RDKit Descriptors

backlog.spec: In addition to the Morgan fingerprint, generate a Count Fingerprint (radius 2) and add its bits to the feature vector. Then, average the outputs of the current RF/XGBoost ensemble with a third model trained on these Count Fingerprints.
backlog.title: Count Fingerprint Blend

backlog.spec: Transform the target labels y from {0, 1} to {log(-1), log(1)} (effectively a logit transform) before training. This is often used in some boosting implementations to stabilize the gradient updates, then transform back to 0-1 probabilities for the final output.
backlog.title: Logit Transform Target

incumbent.description: Average the predict_proba outputs of the existing 300-tree RandomForestClassifier and a new XGBClassifier (max_depth=3, 300 estimators) trained on the same Morgan-plus-descriptor features.

memo: Helped: two accepted changes. Slot 1 added RDKit descriptors (MolWt, MolLogP, NumHDonors) to the Morgan bits: 0.1233 vs the 0.1361 baseline (one run). Slot 15 averaged RF with a second model: 0.1140/0.1098, replicated. The incumbent is 0.1119 over 2 runs. Boosting alone scored 0.1157-0.1189 for XGBoost and 0.1171/0.1162 for LightGBM, so the blend beat it. Not helped: CatBoost (0.1409), RF MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF 4 (0.1279), 1000 trees (0.1218), extra count features (0.1218-0.1228), VarianceThreshold (0.1158), balanced RF (0.1147), blend weight 0.4 (0.1131), stacking (0.1260), 1024 bits (0.1157), XGBoost early stopping (0.1138), subsampling (0.1143). Radius 3 gave 0.1104 (-0.0015), within noise (sd about 0.0049) but the best single run. Next: replicate radius 3 inside the RF+XGBoost blend. Try rank averaging, and add a third diverse model, such as logistic regression or an SVM on count fingerprints. Avoid RF tweaks, single-feature additions and repeating aborted ideas.
